# Gotchas

- billing::Invoice::number — 0 is the reserved "draft/unissued" sentinel; NEVER assign 0 to an issued invoice or the renderer will show it as DRAFT.
- billing::NEXT_INVOICE — must stay >= 1 (starts at 1000, only increments); never reset it to 0 or let it wrap, or issue_number() could hand out the draft sentinel.
- billing::render_invoice — must stay pure/read-only; it must NEVER call issue_number() (previewing a draft would consume a real number from the global sequence each call).
- billing::Invoice::issue — the ONLY sanctioned way to give an invoice a number; constructing an Invoice with a hand-picked number bypasses the 0-means-draft contract (the field is pub, nothing enforces it).

content.text:
Done — `gotchas.md` is in the repo root.

The latent invariant the fix relies on: **`Invoice::number == 0` means "draft"**. The old code in `render_invoice` (src/billing.rs:55) called `issue_number()` whenever it saw a draft, so every preview consumed a fresh number from the global `NEXT_INVOICE` sequence — hence the "different number every time" bug. The fix renders `INVOICE DRAFT` for `number == 0`, which only works because:

1. `issue_number()` can never return 0 — `NEXT_INVOICE` starts at 1000 and only increments (so no reset/wraparound may ever bring it to 0).
2. `render_invoice` must remain read-only — it must never touch the numbering sequence.
3. `Invoice::issue()` is the only sanctioned way to assign a number; since `number` is a `pub` field, nothing stops a caller from hand-setting 0 on a real invoice, which would silently render it as a draft.

`gotchas.md` documents these as four one-line entries referencing `billing::Invoice::number`, `billing::NEXT_INVOICE`, `billing::render_invoice`, and `billing::Invoice::issue`.
